authoredNote: Expectations are hand-derived from the numbered source, THEN compared with a run; the run confirmed every line and is not the source of any value here. Declarations: EXPORTED on 6, SECRET on 10, OVERRIDDEN on 11 and again on 12 (the `override` line carries its own assignment, so ONE name has TWO contains edges), GONE on 13, DYNAMIC on 15, target `all` on 18. Prerequisite references to SECRET and OVERRIDDEN sit on 18, the rule's own line; the recipe's `$(DYNAMIC)` and `$(GONE)` on 19. Line 16 (`vpath %.c src`) is the one line that must produce nothing, and `expectSymbolCount` is what pins that.
rationale: This fixture exists because five constructs the analyzer MODELLED had no test at all — private_directive, override_directive, undefine_directive, unexport_directive and shell_assignment appeared in zero of 99 corpus files, and vpath_directive produced no observable output whatsoever. Untested code is not coverage, and here it was not even correct: three of those paths were broken. (1) `private VAR = v` and `override VAR := v` put the keyword and the assignment on ONE line, and the walker reads the directive before the assignment nested inside it, so the flag was applied to a symbol that did not exist yet and silently dropped — in exactly the spelling people write, while the rarer two-line form worked. (2) `undefine VAR` was a PHANTOM: its operand is a `variable` FIELD holding a bare word with no named children, and the branch searched for a nested `variable_assignment`, so it could never fire — the same failure mode as the dead `endif_directive` branch, which is why that one was found and this one survived, because nothing exercised either. (3) `unexport` cleared only the metadata flag and left the `exports` EDGE, so the graph said the file exports a variable the symbol table said it did not. Each is pinned as a forbidden shape below. The vpath line is pinned POSITIVELY as the pattern `Make vpath` and negatively by `expectSymbolCount`: it records that the file uses a search path while inventing no declaration, because a vpath names directories the file does not declare. Pinning both directions is what separates a deliberate silence from an unimplemented construct.

expectRelationships.note: SECTION B PIN: `OVERRIDDEN := base` (L11) then `override OVERRIDDEN := forced` (L12) is a REDEFINITION, not a new declaration — the ONE construct among make's four silent kinds that exists. Both lines ride the edge (overrideLine/baseLine) so a reader can see which binding is replaced and where; the lane's ruling (real-makefile-analyzer.ts:830-858) refuses the edge when the replaced binding is the command line or the environment, because that is not a symbol in the graph and the edge would dangle by construction.

forbidRelationships.note: THE THIRD DEFECT. `export EXPORTED` on 7 and `unexport EXPORTED` on 8 cancel: the symbol says isExported:false, so this edge must not exist. Pre-fix the flag was cleared and the edge kept, and a consumer reading relationships got the opposite answer from a consumer reading symbols. An unexport retracts the EDGE, not just the flag.
only the TARGET `all` is exported. A `shell_assignment` declaration is not an export, and a spurious one would make every shell-valued variable look published.
